subject.title: fix(infra): release exec-approvals locks across VirtioFS identity drift

question: Should maintainers adopt this localized exec-approvals lock protocol rather than the overlapping proposal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028, after real VirtioFS evidence and an authorization-boundary audit?
rationale: Both open PRs change the same fail-closed authorization lock and claim the same root-cause fix, but they differ in scope and hardening. Selecting the permanent ownership model is a maintainer security/architecture decision rather than a mechanical contributor follow-up.

options.title: Select one canonical proposal after live proof
options.body: Require a redacted affected-environment run and owner audit, then retain only the chosen nonce-lock implementation.

options.title: Prefer the smaller overlapping proposal
options.body: Adopt the narrower implementation from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028 if its claimed live proof and current-main rebase are independently confirmed.

options.title: Move the protocol into fs-safe first
options.body: Pause both OpenClaw-local variants and pursue a separately reviewed upstream lock contract if maintainers want all consumers to share the repair.

recommendation.title: Select one canonical proposal after live proof
recommendation.body: Require a redacted affected-environment run and owner audit, then retain only the chosen nonce-lock implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the production reproduction and own the overlapping candidate, so they are best placed to clarify affected-environment behavior and compare the alternatives.
